title: INFLUENCE OF DIFFERENT BONDING PROTOCOLS FOR ALIGNER ATTACHMENTS ON TRANSFER ACCURACY, LOSS RATE AND ABRASION RESISTANCE - A RANDOMISED CONTROLLED TRIAL
summary: The treatment of tooth misalignments with aligners (transparent, sequential dental splints) is becoming increasingly popular. For the realisation of a variety of different tooth movements, the application of attachments (geometries made of plastic) to the teeth is essential in order to increase the force application area on the one hand, but also to change the force application itself. It is important that these attachments retain their original geometry over the entire treatment period and do not wear out significantly, e.g. due to the insertion and removal of the dental splints, which takes place several times a day, but at least for every meal. Different filled dental composites as well as different bonding techniques are available for attachments. The aim of this study is to investigate in a randomised controlled split-mouth design whether the bonding protocol and thus the material has an influence on the transfer accuracy, loss rate and abrasion resistance and finally on the time needed to remove any excess bonding.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Orthodontic correction planned with aligners (Shark Aligner)
- Attachments necessary in both dental arches
- Permanent dentition
- No severe crowding in the front LII >7
- Signed consent
Exclusion criteria:
- Missing teeth
- Microdont teeth or abnormal shape
- Tooth non-unions (permanent dentition)
- Previous or planned extraction of permanent teeth
- Severe crowding in the front LII>7
- Existing amalgam or gold restorations
- Periodontal / gingival damage (probing depth >3mm or radiologically detectable)
- Craniofacial syndromes/LKG/genetic diseases
- Systemic diseases, increased need for protection
